newsitem.title: USA: Versace killed during murderous week in Miami.
newsitem.headline: Versace killed during murderous week in Miami.

text.p: The slaying of Italian designer Gianni Versace was one of 18 murders in Miami's Dade County last week, one of the most violent weeks in the recent history of a metropolis with a global reputation as a crime capital.

Domestic disputes, deadly street fights and a mass murder on a freighter, along with the shooting death of Versace and the dragnet for the homosexual prostitute serial killer suspected of his murder, made the week of July 13-19 one of Miami's worst.
The Miami Herald said the only other week that produced more homicides was during the 1980 Liberty City race riots, when 27 people died, 14 of them riot-related.
The county, which includes the cities of Miami and Miami Beach, recently has averaged about five murders a week, the newspaper said.

The Metro-Dade Police Department said weekly statistics were not kept. But it was likely some weeks during the heyday of the Colombian cocaine cowboys in the 1980s -- when street shoot-outs were daily fare and Miami gained its "Dodge City" reputation -- produced more homicides, spokesman Pat Brickman said.
"It's high for this period of history, the last five or eight years," he said. "But you go back to the cocaine days of the 80s, there were probably more."

Miami's reputation as a tourist paradise was tarnished by a series of tourist slayings during 1992-93. But Brickman said the county murder rate had actually dropped significantly during the last decade.

On July 14, the day before the Versace slaying, four crew members, three Haitians and a Ghanaian, were killed aboard a Belize-registered freighter at a wharf on the Miami River. Police suspect the murders were drug-related.

The next day, alleged serial killer Andrew Cunanan, a gay prostitute wanted in connection with four murders in northern U.S. states, was believed to have shot Versace twice in the head on the steps of his Miami Beach palazzo.
More than a week later, a nationwide manhunt has failed to find Cunanan, known as a master of disguise who police say may be dressing as a woman to evade capture.

Last Thursday, five people were slain including Silvio Alfonso, a Miami Springs doctor. FBI agents rushed to the scene after a neighbour reported seeing a man resembling Cunanan fleeing. Investigators ultimately discounted a link to the Versace slaying and later arrested a suspect who was wearing Alfonso's clothes.

Police were also investigating the stabbing of a man by a relative during a family reunion, a shooting during a dice game, and the death of a man found floating in the water with his hands and feet tied.
